rules.name: No privileged identity
rules.description: The HAP must install as an ordinary application. Adding a requestPermissions entry beyond ohos.permission.INTERNET, adding an ACL list or an elevated APL, setting app-feature to hos_system_app, or calling an API the ArkTS compiler flags as a system API all violate this.

rules.name: No secret in the repository
rules.description: No API key, token, password or private key may be added to a tracked file. The model API key is entered on the device and stored in device preferences. scripts/check-secrets.sh enforces this in the default test gate.

rules.name: The engine stays platform-agnostic
rules.description: Files under core/ must not import from @kit.* or @ohos.*, and must not perform HTTP directly. All network access goes through the injected LlmTransport interface, because that is what keeps the engine testable without an SDK.

rules.name: Degradation is labelled and nothing throws
rules.description: An expected failure - network error, timeout, HTTP error, malformed model output, a dropped placeholder - must return a RewriteOutcome with source 'local' and a non-empty fallbackReason that the keyboard renders. A new throw on an expected failure path, or a fallback that leaves the reason empty, violates this.

rules.name: Documentation is backed by the code
rules.description: No feature may be described in README.md or under docs/ that does not exist in the code. Test counts, the status table, and capability claims must match what the repository actually contains.

rules.name: Observed behaviour is separated from expectation
rules.description: A behaviour may be described as verified only when it was observed on the emulator, with the evidence committed under docs/evidence/. Anything unverified must be marked as unverified, and values copied from documentation rather than tested must be labelled expected rather than verified.

rules.name: The system is not modified
rules.description: The deliverable is an installable component that adds a capability without modifying the operating system. No OpenHarmony source patch, no replaced system bundle, and no instruction to flash an image.
